ai.title: Add logger to getUserInfoFromApiKey and SDK runtime
ai.summary: Updated `getUserInfoFromApiKey` contract to require a `logger` instance, propagating it through backend auth checks, websocket handlers, and web API endpoints. Implemented `CLI_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL` and SDK-specific database client in `sdk/src/impl/` to support local agent execution. The new SDK implementation calls `/api/v1/me` with Bearer auth, handling errors via the injected logger.

eli5.text: When you send your API key to the service, the system now creates a written record of what happens during that check, so problems can be traced later instead of silently failing. This logging is now passed along automatically to every place that verifies an API key, including the real-time connections and web requests. If you looked at the code today, you'd see the assistant tools for the SDK gaining the ability to run locally with database access, though the main visible difference is the improved error reporting path.

ai.title: SDK fetchAgentFromDatabase implemented, apiKey threaded through
ai.summary: SDK `fetchAgentFromDatabase` implemented in `sdk/src/impl/database.ts`, hitting `/api/v1/agents/{publisher}/{id}/{version}` with Bearer token. `apiKey` added to `AgentRuntimeScopedDeps` and `FetchAgentFromDatabaseFn` params, propagated through `WebSocketMiddleware`, `evals/scaffolding.ts`, and `validate-agent-name.ts`. `getAgentTemplate` now spreads scoped params into `fetchAgentFromDatabase` calls. Test runtime `TEST_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL` merged with `TEST_AGENT_RUNTIME_SCOPED_IMPL`.

eli5.text: Starting today, when you ask the assistant to pull up an agent from the database, it will securely send along your API key as a bearer token, so the backend can verify you're allowed to see that agent and return it. If you're running tests or using the web-socket tools, the same key now travels with the request automatically instead of being left out. Behind the scenes, the code that fetches agent templates passes this key through wherever it needs to, and the test setup was combined so both old and new checks use the same key handling. The feature is live now for anyone authenticating through the supported entry points.

ai.title: SDK implements startAgentRun
ai.summary: SDK implements `startAgentRun` via POST to `/api/v1/agent-runs`. `StartAgentRunFn` contract now requires `apiKey`, returns `string | null`. `run-agent-step.ts` passes expanded params to `startAgentRun`. `CLI_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL` now includes `startAgentRun`.

eli5.text: When you start a new run of an AI agent through the SDK, the system now sends the request to a dedicated endpoint using your API key, and the call returns a run ID you can track. If the request succeeds, the agent gets a unique identifier for that run; if it fails, the system returns nothing instead of crashing. This affects anyone using the SDK to launch agent runs programmatically, who will now provide their API key at startup and receive a run ID back (or a clear failure). The behavior is live today, since the SDK implementation is wired into the CLI agent runtime.

ai.title: run-agent-step uses startAgentRun return runId
ai.summary: run-agent-step.ts now uses the runId returned by startAgentRun instead of generating one via crypto.randomUUID. If startAgentRun returns no runId, the loop throws Failed to start agent run. Scope limited to packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts. runId assignment to agentState moved after the return value check.

eli5.text: When the agent runtime starts a new step in its execution loop, it now obtains the run identifier directly from the service that starts the agent run, rather than generating its own placeholder identifier and guessing the assignment. If that service does not return a valid identifier, the loop stops and surfaces a clear failure instead of continuing with an empty or guessed value. You would notice this only if you were inspecting internal logs or debugging why an agent run halted unexpectedly: the failure message now names the reason rather than silently carrying a blank identifier. The change is live in this version of the runtime package.

ai.title: SDK: Implement finishAgentRun and fix URL construction
ai.summary: Added `finishAgentRun` to the SDK, wiring it into `CLI_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL` and updating `FinishAgentRunFn` to require `apiKey`. Implemented `POST /api/v1/agent-runs` with `action: 'FINISH'` to report run status and credits. Refactored URL construction in `database.ts` to use `new URL(path, base)` instead of string concatenation. This change affects the SDK's agent lifecycle management and database contract types.

eli5.text: The assistant can now cleanly sign off on a run and report its final status and credit usage, the same way it already signs in to start one. Behind the scenes, it talks to a single, correct web address instead of building the URL by sticking pieces together like a word puzzle, which makes that reporting more reliable. Nothing about what you see changes yet, but the machinery that closes out a session is now in place and wired up alongside the rest of the agent lifecycle.

ai.title: SDK CLI agent runtime implements consumeCreditsWithFallback
ai.summary: SDK CLI agent runtime now implements `consumeCreditsWithFallback` in `sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts`. The function returns a success object with `chargedToOrganization: false`, replacing the previous omission from `CLI_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL`. This change ensures the CLI agent runtime provides a concrete billing fallback mechanism.

eli5.text: The assistant's built-in helper can now report what happens when it runs out of credits, instead of just stopping. It will say that your personal account is not being charged and your company's organization is not billed either. If you saw it fail before when credits ran out, you would now see a clearer signal that the task paused rather than crashed.

ai.title: Fix loopAgentSteps typecheck by spreading params into finishAgentRun
ai.summary: Typecheck fix in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`. `loopAgentSteps` now spreads `params` into `finishAgentRun` calls instead of passing explicit `userId` and `logger`. This resolves type errors caused by missing parameters in `finishAgentRun` signature. Internal refactor only.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a run of automated steps, it now pulls all the needed details from a single bundle instead of grabbing them piece by piece. This smooths out a behind-the-scenes mismatch that had been causing type-checking errors during the step-by-step loop. Regular users will notice nothing different; it's the equivalent of quietly reorganizing a workspace so tools fit together properly.

ai.title: Fix backend unit tests for validate-agent-name
ai.summary: Updated validate-agent-name.test.ts to use expect.objectContaining for handler spy assertions. Removed strict equality checks on the logger argument to accommodate non-deterministic logger instances. Scope limited to backend test suite.

eli5.text: The backend tests for checking agent names are now less strict about how they verify the logging details. If you looked at the test code, you would see that it no longer demands the logger be passed in a very specific way - instead, it just checks the important parts like the agent ID and version. This makes the tests more reliable without changing any features you would notice in the product.

ai.title: Add iterative orchestrator agents
ai.summary: Introduces iterative-orchestrator and iterative-orchestrator-step agents to decompose large tasks into parallelizable batches. Updates base2-implementor-gpt-5.ts ID to match filename and adjusts research-implement-orchestrator.ts spawnableAgents accordingly. Implements stateful planning loop in iterative-orchestrator.ts using structured output and spawn_agents tool.

eli5.text: A coding assistant can now split a big project into smaller, independent chunks and tackle them in parallel, rather than working through one piece at a time. When you give it a large task, it plans the work in rounds, hands each round's pieces to specialist helpers, and keeps going until the whole job is done, so large jobs finish faster. This new planning and parallel-execution capability is live today for the internal orchestrator agents, and one existing helper was renamed so it matches its actual configuration file. If you look, you would see the orchestrator calling multiple helpers at once instead of waiting for each step to complete before starting the next.

ai.title: Update nightly evals to compare base and base2-fast
ai.summary: Nightly buffbench configuration in `evals/buffbench/main-nightly.ts` updated. Agents list changed from `['base', 'base-lite-grok-4-fast']` to `['base', 'base2-fast']`. Scope limited to eval pipeline. No impact on production model pickers or user-facing features.

eli5.text: Each night, the team runs a set of automated tests that check how well two different AI assistants perform at coding tasks. They swapped out one of the assistants in those nightly tests called base-lite-grok-4-fast and replaced it with a new one called base2-fast. This only affects the internal testing system; it doesn't change anything you see or use, and it doesn't impact which AI you get when you sign in.

ai.title: Iterative orchestrator switches to base2-with-files-input
ai.summary: New `base2-with-files-input` agent replaces `base2-fast` in `iterative-orchestrator.ts` execution steps. This agent explicitly reads files via `read_files` and runs `context-pruner` before each step to manage context. Orchestrator now enforces a 15-iteration limit with dynamic reminders injected into prompts. `successCriteria` removed from step schema; `filesToReadHints` and `notes` descriptions updated in `iterative-orchestrator-step.ts` to guide smaller, validated changes.

eli5.text: The system that breaks big coding jobs into smaller steps has quietly switched the helper it uses to do the actual work, so each step now has the helper explicitly open the relevant files first and ask a separate tool to clean up unused information before proceeding. The new helper also stops itself after 15 tries to avoid running forever, and the people planning each step now write smaller, clearer goals instead of listing separate success conditions. If you used this system, you would notice that each step reads the files it needs up front and the whole job is less likely to stall on its own; behind the scenes, the instructions for planning steps were also reworded to nudge the helper toward smaller, safer changes.

ai.title: Refactor CLI agent runtime to lazy factory
ai.summary: The `CLI_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL` constant is replaced by a `getAgentRuntimeImpl` factory function in `sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts`. This allows passing a `logger` and `apiKey` as parameters, removing the hard dependency on `process.env.CODEBUFF_API_KEY` and default no-op logger at module load time.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant from the command line, it now figures out how to connect to its backend services a little later in the process, after your login key and any logging setup are already in hand. Before, those credentials were read from your environment right when the program loaded, so the tool always expected your secret key to be waiting in a specific spot from the very first moment. You won't notice a visual difference in what the assistant does, but the tool is now more forgiving about where that key comes from and can accept alternative logging setup if one is provided.

ai.title: Implement addAgentStep in SDK
ai.summary: Implemented addAgentStep in sdk/src/impl/database.ts to POST step data to /api/v1/agent-runs/{id}/steps. Updated AddAgentStepFn contract in common/src/types/contracts/database.ts to require apiKey and return Promise<string | null>. Agent runtime now passes full params to addAgentStep, replacing manual field destructuring in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts.

eli5.text: The agent can now automatically record each of its work steps (including credits used, status, and any errors) to your run history as it goes, instead of skipping that logging. When you run an agent, it now sends its full context, including your access key, to the logging step rather than manually picking individual fields, so fewer details get dropped along the way. This is live today for anyone running an agent through the SDK.

ai.title: SDK wires addAgentStep into agent runtime
ai.summary: addAgentStep wired into getAgentRuntimeImpl in sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts. Omit<AgentRuntimeDeps & AgentRuntimeScopedDeps, ...> drops 'addAgentStep' from excluded keys, and impl now returns addAgentStep directly instead of commented stub. Scope limited to SDK agent runtime deps. Previously addAgentStep was omitted from the returned deps object.

eli5.text: Developers who build agents with the software kit can now include a real 'add a step' capability when they set up an agent's runtime, instead of leaving it out. If you look at the setup code today, you'll see that capability is wired in directly rather than sitting as a placeholder comment, so agents created with the SDK have access to adding steps as part of their built-in behaviors.

ai.title: SDK 0.4.5 adds SIGKILL fallback for terminal command timeout
ai.summary: Version bump to 0.4.5 in `sdk/package.json`. `run-terminal-command.ts` adds fallback to `SIGKILL` if `SIGTERM` fails during timeout. Ensures processes terminate reliably when unresponsive. Scope limited to SDK tool execution logic.

eli5.text: When a command you run through the SDK takes too long, it first tries to stop it politely with a standard signal. If that polite attempt fails or the command ignores it, it now forcefully kills the process instead of leaving it hanging. You'd notice this if a command that normally would have hung or timed out now reliably finishes instead of lingering. This improves reliability of terminal command execution within the SDK.

ai.title: Version 1.0.503 ships SDK agent lifecycle and runtime updates
ai.summary: Version 1.0.503 of the CLI bumps npm-app/release/package.json from 1.0.502 to 1.0.503 as a release packaging update. This release bundles the 2025-10-22 SDK work including finishAgentRun POST with action FINISH, consumeCreditsWithFallback returning chargedToOrganization false, startAgentRun requiring apiKey returning string null, addAgentStep posting to /api/v1/agent-runs/{id}/steps, and SIGKILL fallback in run-terminal-command on timeout. Additional notable 2025-10-21 to 2025-10-22 changes include lazy getAgentRuntimeImpl factory replacing CLI_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL constant, fetch injected into AgentRuntimeDeps binding globalThis.fetch in backend evals runtimes, and trackEvent injected into agent runtime deps.
ai.evidence: The diff in npm-app/release/package.json changes the "version" field from "1.0.502" to "1.0.503". The commit analysis notes list 2025-10-22 SDK agent lifecycle and runtime updates, including finishAgentRun, consumeCreditsWithFallback, startAgentRun, addAgentStep, and SIGKILL fallback.

eli5.text: Version 1.0.503 adds full agent-run lifecycle tracking, new planner and orchestrator agents, and a more stable SDK with better text streaming. You can now start, record steps for, and finish agent runs through new web API endpoints, and the CLI and SDK share the same robust streaming logic that prevents duplicated or missing text in responses. The release introduces hybrid planning agents that combine GPT-5 and Claude models to decompose complex coding tasks into research and implementation phases, alongside an iterative orchestrator that breaks large jobs into parallelizable batches with enforced iteration limits. Terminal command output is now consistently truncated at 50,000 characters for both stdout and stderr, the backend no longer crashes on uncaught exceptions, and the CLI binary download is proxied through a new endpoint so future download source changes won't break existing clients. Upgrading gives you faster, more reliable agent runs with clearer progress tracking, better error resilience, and access to newer planning models like GPT-5 and Gemini Flash Lite.

ai.title: Hide context-pruner subagent output in CLI
ai.summary: New `shouldHideAgent` utility filters `codebuff/context-pruner` subagent events from the CLI UI. `use-send-message.ts` skips rendering `subagent_start` and `subagent_finish` events for hidden agents, preventing their logs and stream accumulators from appearing. Scope limited to `cli/src/utils/constants.ts` and `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`. Matching uses substring check against `HIDDEN_AGENT_IDS`.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant, it quietly calls on a background helper called the context-pruner to tidy up long conversations. Starting today, that helper's status messages and progress logs no longer flash across your terminal screen. If you watched the CLI output, you'd notice those background lines are missing, even though the pruning work is still happening behind the scenes.

ai.title: CLI loads local agent definitions from .agents directory
ai.summary: Added `loadAgentDefinitions` in `cli/src/utils/load-agent-definitions.ts` to parse `.agents` directories. `useSendMessage` hook updated to inject these definitions into SDK `client.run` calls. Supports custom agent logic via local TypeScript files.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant from a project folder, it will now look for a hidden folder named.agents in that folder or any folder above it. If it finds custom agent instructions written there as plain text files, the assistant loads those and uses them instead of its default behavior, letting you keep specialized assistant setups per project without changing global settings. You would notice this the first time you launch the assistant in a folder that contains a.agents directory; nothing changes for folders that do not have one.

ai.title: Add FAST/MAX agent mode toggle to CLI
ai.summary: Added an interactive toggle for agent mode in the CLI interface, switchable via Shift+Tab or mouse click. The selected mode determines the backend agent used for each request ('base2-fast' or 'base2-max'). State management updated in chat-store.ts to persist the mode, while chat.tsx and use-send-message.ts handle the UI integration and request routing.

eli5.text: When you're chatting with the assistant in the CLI, you can now choose between two modes: a quicker, simpler mode (shown in green as FAST) or a more powerful, thorough mode (shown in red as 💪 MAX). You switch between them by clicking the colored label or pressing the Shift and Tab keys at the same time. Whatever mode is shown when you send a message is the one the assistant will use to answer you, and your last choice stays set for future chats.

ai.title: Ghostty detection defaults to dark mode
ai.summary: Theme system detects Ghostty terminal and defaults to dark mode. Fast mode toggle background color adjusted to #0a6515. Code formatting and minor refactoring in theme-system.ts and agent-mode-toggle.tsx.

eli5.text: If you use Ghostty, the terminal now automatically uses a dark color theme instead of needing you to set it manually. The fast-mode toggle button also got slightly greener, so the bright green "FAST" label looks a bit darker now. These visual tweaks are live today for anyone running the CLI on Ghostty.

ai.title: SDK implements promptAiSdkStream, provider options loop, runId rename
ai.summary: sdk implements promptAiSdkStream using @ai-sdk/openai-compatible against /api/v1. common/util/messages.ts loops provider keys (anthropic, openrouter, codebuff) for cacheControl set/delete. backend/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts loops openrouter/codebuff for reasoning exclude. common/types/contracts/database.ts renames agentRunId to runId. common/types/contracts/llm.ts adds apiKey to PromptAiSdkStreamFn. packages/agent-runtime/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts accepts apiKey, loops provider options for reasoning. sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts wires local promptAiSdkStream. web/src/api/v1/chat/completions.ts reads codebuff_metadata.run_id.

eli5.text: The assistant can now stream answers through the software development kit, which means programs embedded inside other apps can tap into the same live, word-by-word answer flow that the main web version uses. Behind it, the system now talks to three AI service names at once and reads the correct license key up front, so third-party integrations no longer have to guess which provider settings apply. If you build or run such an embedded app, your streamed answers will behave the same as the browser version instead of falling back to a simpler mode.

ai.title: Implement promptAiSdk in SDK
ai.summary: Added non-streaming `promptAiSdk` function to `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` using `generateText` from the `ai` package. Updated `PromptAiSdkFn` contract in `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts` to require `apiKey`. Wired `promptAiSdk` into `sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts` dependencies and provided dummy `apiKey` values in `evals/git-evals/gen-evals.ts` and `scripts/get-changelog.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now get a straight answer all at once instead of watching it type word by word, when the underlying model is asked directly through the software development kit. Previously only the live, word-by-word mode was wired up in the kit; now a second, one-shot path has been connected and the security token (formerly optional) is required on every call, so any integration that skips it will stop working. For everyday users of the finished product nothing looks different, because the new route is already in place behind the scenes and the older streaming behavior still drives what you see.

ai.title: Implement promptAiSdkStructured in SDK
ai.summary: Added `promptAiSdkStructured` to `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` using `generateObject` for typed responses. Updated `PromptAiSdkStructuredInput` in `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts` to require `apiKey`. Eval scripts in `evals/git-evals/` patched to pass dummy API keys.

eli5.text: If you ask the AI coding assistant for information that should come back in a predictable, structured format, it can now receive that information more reliably instead of as a free-form answer. The system added a new way to handle these structured requests that requires an API key, and updated the supporting evaluation tools and type checks to go along with it. This means the responses will match the expected format, and anything that relied on the old setup has been adjusted to pass along the necessary API key. This is already available in the current version.

ai.title: SDK: wire promptAiSdkStructured into agent runtime
ai.summary: promptAiSdkStructured added to getAgentRuntimeImpl return object in sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts. Import extended from './llm'; prior Omit exclusion and commented placeholder removed. Structured-output LLM path now available to agent runtime consumers alongside promptAiSdk and promptAiSdkStream. SDK package only; no CLI or Web surface change.

eli5.text: If you're building an app with the developer kit, your assistant can now receive a complete, structured answer from the AI in one go instead of getting it piece by piece. Behind the scenes, the developer kit turned on a previously prepared code path that delivers the full answer at once, which some tasks prefer over the older streaming option. This is available to anyone using the developer kit's built-in agent tools today; the change only affects the developer kit, not the web interface or command-line tools.

ai.title: CLI Staging Deploy Refactor
ai.summary: Staging deploys now trigger on pushes and PRs containing '[codecane]'. CI uses Bun instead of Node. New composite action setup-project centralizes Bun setup and caching. Windows builds removed from CLI release matrix.

eli5.text: Staging deploys for the CLI tool now happen automatically whenever someone pushes code or opens a pull request that includes the tag '[codecane]'. The build process switched from using Node to using Bun, which is a faster JavaScript runtime, and a new shared setup step was added to handle Bun installation and caching. Windows was dropped from the release build targets, so releases are now built only for Linux and macOS. These changes are live today for the CLI staging environment.

ai.title: Remove processStream from SDK
ai.summary: Deleted sdk/src/process-stream.ts, removing the processStream helper that spawned CODEBUFF_BINARY and parsed stdout/stderr into PrintModeEvent objects. This eliminates the child_process wrapper and JSON line-buffering logic from the SDK surface. No replacement mechanism is visible in the diff.

eli5.text: The SDK no longer includes a helper that used to run an external binary and turn its text output into structured events you could react to in real time. If you relied on that streaming bridge between the SDK and the binary, it is gone, and the diff shows no replacement being added in the same snapshot. Other SDK capabilities around agent runs and logging are still being wired up, but this specific streaming path is deleted.
